newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA LEU LITTLE CHANGED, MARKET CONFUSED.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA LEU LITTLE CHANGED, MARKET CONFUSED.

text.p: Romania's leu closed Wednesday near 6,950 to the dollar, slightly firmer than 7,000 at opening amid slaken interbank activity, traders said.
Most dealers said their clients were confused by a central bank decision on Tuesday to release the leu rate for each day, which replaces the former reference rate, only once weekly.
"My clients were mixed up because the central bank (BNR) decision lacks clarity," said one trader, adding that most companies had previously used the reference rate to reflect deals in book-keeping.

On Tuesday, the BNR said it had replaced the old reference rate, which served for statistical and accounting purposes, and would compute a daily exchange rate for the leu as an average of prices on the local market.
It said companies would have to use in book-keeping the exchange rates set by the banks where they hold their accounts.

On Wednesday, central bank officials declined to elaborate further on Tuesday's move saying details would be available on Friday when BNR governor Mugur Isarescu was expected to hold a news conference.

The new rate, to be used only for statistical purposes, would be sent daily to the Finance Ministry, the customs as well as to the prosecutor's office and the police. A list of daily rates would be released weekly to the media.
Dealers said short-term rates bobbed near 220 percent but most of them were reluctant to predict trends on the foreign exchange and money markets.
"What can I say? The leu inched up although the money market doesn't face leu shortages. I don't know where the leu gets its support from," said one dealer.
Banks' quotes floated in wide ranges, with leu-dollar prices from 6,200/100 to 7,400/8,400.
Leu-dollar retail rates inched down towards 7,300/800 from some 7,100/400 in early trading hours.
